LAB-001.q: Under the 2019 Labour Code, labour contracts are of the following types:
o: Indefinite-term contracts and fixed-term contracts of up to 36 months
Three types including seasonal contracts under 12 months
LAB-001.e: The 2019 Labour Code abolished seasonal contracts, leaving 2 types.
LAB-001.x:
Basis: Article 20 of Labour Code 45/2019/QH14.
Analysis: The 2019 Code has only two contract types: indefinite and fixed-term up to 36 months; the 2012 seasonal/task contracts under 12 months were abolished.
Distractors: B is the old rule; C and D are wrong (probation isn't a contract type).

LAB-002.q: Labour contracts of 1 month or more must be concluded in writing or electronically as data messages.
LAB-002.e: True. Electronic contracts have the same value as written ones.
LAB-002.x:
Basis: Article 14 of the 2019 Labour Code; 2023 E-Transactions Law.
Analysis: True. Contracts of 1 month or more must be written or electronic data messages (equivalent to writing); shorter ones may be oral (with exceptions).

LAB-003.q: Match each job position with the maximum probation period:
p: Job requiring college degree or higher
Job requiring intermediate level, technical worker, professional staff
LAB-003.e: Article 25 of the 2019 Labour Code; probation only once per job.
LAB-003.x:
Basis: Article 25 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Maximum probation: enterprise managers 180 days; college-level and above 60 days; intermediate, technical workers, clerical staff 30 days; other work 6 working days. One probation per job.

LAB-004.q: The salary for an accountant position is VND 15 million/month. What is the statutory minimum probation salary (VND)?
LAB-004.e: At least 85% of the job salary: 15,000,000 × 85% = 12,750,000 VND.
LAB-004.x:
Basis: Article 26 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Working: Probation pay is at least 85% of the job's salary: 15,000,000 × 85% = 12,750,000 VND.

LAB-005.q: Probation does not apply to employees with labour contracts of less than 1 month.
LAB-005.e: True under Article 24 of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-005.x:
Basis: Article 24 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Contracts under 1 month have no probation – too short for a trial period.

LAB-006.q: Match the contract type with the minimum notice period for employee unilateral termination (ordinary case):
LAB-006.e: Certain special occupations have longer notice periods set by the Government.
LAB-006.x:
Basis: Article 35 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Employee resignation (ordinary): indefinite contracts – 45 days' notice; 12–36-month fixed term – 30 days; under 12 months – 3 working days. No reason is needed, but notice must be respected.

LAB-007.q: Select ALL cases where the employee may terminate unilaterally WITHOUT notice:
o: Not paid in full or on time (except force majeure)
A pregnant employee required to stop work by a medical facility
Wants to move to a higher-paying company
Not assigned the agreed job or workplace
LAB-007.e: Changing jobs for personal reasons still requires notice.
LAB-007.x:
Basis: Article 35(2) of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: No notice is needed when: (A) wages aren't paid fully or on time; (B) sexual harassment; (C) a pregnant worker must stop on medical advice; (E) not assigned the agreed job or place (also abuse, forced labour, retirement age…).
Distractors: (D) Leaving for personal reasons still requires notice.

LAB-008.q: Severance allowance for each year of work (periods not covered by UI and not yet paid) equals:
LAB-008.e: Article 46 of the 2019 Labour Code. The salary basis is the average of the 6 months before termination.
LAB-008.x:
Basis: Article 46 of the 2019 Labour Code; Decree 145/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: Severance = half a month's pay per year worked, excluding unemployment-insured periods and years already compensated; pay is the 6-month average before leaving.
Distractors: B is the job-loss allowance rate; C and D are wrong.

LAB-009.q: An employee worked 6 years in total, 4 of which were covered by UI; average salary for the last 6 months is VND 10 million. What is the severance allowance (VND)?
LAB-009.e: Qualifying period = 6 − 4 = 2 years. Allowance = 2 × ½ × 10 million = 10,000,000 VND.
LAB-009.x:
Basis: Article 46 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Working: Countable time = 6 − 4 (unemployment-insured) = 2 years. Severance = 2 × ½ × 10 million = 10,000,000 VND.
Note: Unemployment-insured time is covered by the fund, so severance mostly arises for pre-2009 service or uninsured periods.

LAB-010.q: Job-loss allowance (due to restructuring, technological change, economic reasons…) is paid at:
o: One month's salary per year of work, but at least two months' salary
Half a month's salary per year
LAB-010.x:
Basis: Article 47 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Job-loss allowance (restructuring, technology, economic reasons, mergers…): one month's pay per year worked, at least two months – higher than severance as the job loss isn't the employee's fault.
Distractors: B is severance; C and D are wrong.

LAB-011.q: Enterprises may not unilaterally terminate or dismiss female employees because of marriage, pregnancy, maternity leave or raising a child under 12 months.
LAB-011.e: True, except where the enterprise ceases operations.
LAB-011.x:
Basis: Articles 37(3) and 137 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Employers may not terminate or dismiss women for marriage, pregnancy, maternity leave or nursing a child under 12 months; exceptions include the business ceasing operations (or an individual employer's death or incapacity).

LAB-012.q: On termination, both parties must settle all related payments within 14 working days (extendable up to 30 days in certain cases).
LAB-012.e: True under Article 48 of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-012.x:
Basis: Article 48 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Within 14 working days of termination, both sides settle all amounts (wages, allowances, untaken leave…); up to 30 days for closures, restructuring, disasters… The employer also returns documents and completes social insurance confirmation.

LAB-013.q: A contract under another name (e.g., 'collaborator contract') that involves paid work under one party's management, direction and supervision is still a labour contract.
LAB-013.e: True under Article 13 of the 2019 Labour Code — a compliance risk for SI and PIT when contracts are mislabelled.
LAB-013.x:
Basis: Article 13 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Substance governs: paid work under management and supervision is an employment contract even if called 'collaborator' or 'service'. Consequences: compulsory social insurance, progressive PIT withholding (if 3 months or more) and other labour rights.

LAB-014.q: When a fixed-term contract expires and the employee keeps working without a new contract within 30 days:
o: The contract becomes an indefinite-term contract
It is automatically extended by 36 months
LAB-014.e: Article 20 of the 2019 Labour Code; only one more fixed-term contract may be signed (with exceptions).
LAB-014.x:
Basis: Article 20(2) of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: If a fixed-term contract expires, the employee keeps working and no new contract is signed within 30 days, it becomes indefinite.
Distractors: B, C and D are wrong; seasonal contracts no longer exist.

LAB-015.q: An enterprise may sign at most 2 consecutive fixed-term contracts with the same employee; the third must be indefinite-term (with certain exceptions).
LAB-015.e: True. Exceptions: elderly workers, foreigners, directors hired in state-owned enterprises…
LAB-015.x:
Basis: Article 20(2)(b) of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Only one further fixed-term contract may be signed (max two in a row); the third must be indefinite. Exceptions: elderly workers, foreigners, directors hired for State enterprises, union officials…

LAB-016.q: An enterprise may keep employees' original diplomas/certificates or require a deposit to secure the labour contract.
LAB-016.e: False. Article 17 of the 2019 Labour Code prohibits keeping identity papers and original diplomas and requiring money or asset guarantees.
LAB-016.x:
Basis: Article 17 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: False. Employers may not keep original ID papers, diplomas or certificates, demand cash or asset security, or force work to repay debts. Violations are penalised under Decree 283/2026.

LAB-017.q: The maximum normal working hours under the 2019 Labour Code are:
o: No more than 8 hours/day and 48 hours/week
No more than 10 hours/day and 60 hours/week
No more than 8 hours/day and a mandatory 40 hours/week
LAB-017.e: The State encourages a 40-hour working week.
LAB-017.x:
Basis: Article 105 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Normal hours are at most 8 per day and 48 per week; weekly schedules allow up to 10 hours a day. The State encourages a 40-hour week.
Distractors: B and D exceed limits; C – 40 hours is encouraged, not mandatory.

LAB-018.q: Match the overtime limits under the 2019 Labour Code:
p: No more than 50% of normal working hours
Per year (certain sectors such as textiles, agricultural processing…)
LAB-018.e: Article 107 of the 2019 Labour Code and Article 61 of Decree 145/2020/ND-CP.
LAB-018.x:
Basis: Article 107 of the 2019 Labour Code; Article 61 of Decree 145/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: Overtime: at most 50% of normal daily hours; 40 hours a month; 200 hours a year; up to 300 hours a year in some sectors (textiles, footwear, electronics, farm/forestry/fishery processing…).

LAB-019.q: Match the overtime timing with the minimum pay rate:
p: Public holidays, Tet, paid days off
LAB-019.x:
Basis: Article 98 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Minimum overtime pay: weekdays 150%; weekly rest days 200%; holidays and paid leave days 300% (plus holiday pay). Night work in normal hours: at least +30%; night overtime also gets +20% of daytime pay.

LAB-020.q: A garment worker earns VND 50,000 per hour and works 10 hours of overtime on a normal day. What is the minimum overtime pay (VND)?
LAB-020.x:
Basis: Article 98 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Working: 50,000 × 150% × 10 = 750,000 VND.
Note: From 2026 all of it is PIT-exempt if compliant (PIT-029).

LAB-021.q: At VND 50,000/hour, a worker does 8 hours of overtime on a weekly day off. What is the minimum overtime pay (VND)?
LAB-021.x:
Basis: Labour Code 2019 Art. 98 (overtime pay); Decree 145/2020/ND-CP Art. 55.
Working: Weekly rest day: at least 200% of the rate: 50,000 × 200% × 8 hours = 800,000 VND.
Analysis: Minimums: normal days 150%; weekly rest days 200%; public holidays and paid leave days 300% (plus the holiday's own pay). Night overtime adds 30% plus 20% of daytime pay. The premium above normal pay is PIT-exempt.
Check: 50,000 × 2 = 100,000 per hour × 8 = 800,000 ✓.

LAB-022.q: A plant operator is on duty for 8 hours on National Day (VND 50,000/hour). Apart from full holiday pay, what is the minimum overtime pay (VND)?
LAB-022.e: 50,000 × 300% × 8 = 1,200,000 VND (plus holiday pay, at least 400% in total).
LAB-022.x:
Basis: Article 98 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Working: Holiday overtime = 50,000 × 300% × 8 = 1,200,000 VND; plus holiday pay (100% = 400,000) → at least 1,600,000 VND (400%).

LAB-023.q: A worker does an 8-hour night shift (normal hours) at VND 50,000/hour. What is the minimum night-shift pay (VND)?
LAB-023.x:
Basis: Articles 98 and 106 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Working: Night shift in normal hours: 50,000 × (100% + 30%) × 8 = 520,000 VND.

LAB-024.q: Night work under the 2019 Labour Code is counted from:
LAB-024.x:
Basis: Article 106 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Night work is 22:00 to 06:00 the next day (PIT-030).
Distractors: B and C have wrong hours; D – employers can't define it themselves.

LAB-025.q: From 2026, the total number of paid public holidays and Tet days per year is:
LAB-025.e: New Year 1; Lunar New Year 5; Hung Kings 1; 30/4: 1; 1/5: 1; National Day 2; Vietnam Culture Day 24/11: 1. Total 12 days.
LAB-025.x:
Basis: Resolution 28/2026/QH16; Article 112 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: From 2026 paid holidays: New Year 1; Lunar New Year 5; Hung Kings 1; 30/4: 1; 1/5: 1; National Day 2; Vietnam Culture Day 24/11: 1 → 12 days (previously 11).
Distractors: 11 days predates Resolution 28/2026; 10 and 13 are wrong.

LAB-026.q: On 24/11/2026 (Vietnam Culture Day), employees are entitled to a paid day off under Resolution 28/2026/QH16.
LAB-026.e: True. Resolution 28/2026/QH16 was passed on 24/4/2026, effective 01/7/2026.
LAB-026.x:
Basis: Resolution 28/2026/QH16.
Analysis: True. Resolution 28/2026 (passed 24/04/2026, effective 01/07/2026) makes Vietnam Culture Day, 24/11, a paid holiday – first observed on 24/11/2026. Working that day earns holiday overtime at 300%.

LAB-027.q: Match working conditions with annual paid leave (12 full months):
LAB-027.e: Article 113 of the 2019 Labour Code; one extra day for every 5 years of service (Article 114).
LAB-027.x:
Basis: Articles 113 and 114 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Annual leave (full year): normal 12 working days; minors, disabled workers, hazardous jobs 14; especially hazardous 16. Plus 1 day for every full 5 years with the same employer.

LAB-028.q: An accountant working in normal conditions has worked continuously for 11 years at the company. How many days of annual leave do they get?
LAB-028.e: 12 days + 2 days (1 extra day per 5 full years: 11 years → 2 days) = 14 days.
LAB-028.x:
Basis: Labour Code 2019 Art. 113 (annual leave), Art. 114 (seniority leave); Decree 145/2020/ND-CP.
Working: Normal conditions: 12 working days a year; each full 5 years with the same employer adds 1 day: ⌊11 / 5⌋ = 2 days → 12 + 2 = 14 days.
Analysis: Heavy or hazardous work, minors or disabled workers: 14 days; especially heavy work: 16 days (before seniority). Unused days are paid out on leaving.
Check: The third extra day comes only at year 15 ✓.

LAB-029.q: Match the personal event with the leave entitlement under the 2019 Labour Code:
LAB-029.e: Article 115 of the 2019 Labour Code. Death of a parent, spouse or child: 3 days fully paid.
LAB-029.x:
Basis: Article 115 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Paid leave: own marriage 3 days; child's marriage 1 day; death of parents (including in-laws), spouse or child 3 days. Unpaid 1 day (with notice): death of grandparents or siblings; marriage of parents or siblings.

LAB-030.q: Employees working 8 continuous hours get a break of at least 30 minutes (at least 45 minutes at night), counted as working time.
LAB-030.e: True under Article 109 of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-030.x:
Basis: Article 109 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Continuous work of 6 or more hours (as regulated) gets at least a 30-minute break, 45 minutes at night; breaks count as working time.

LAB-031.q: Enterprises may not assign pregnant female employees from the 7th month (or 6th month in highland, remote, border or island areas) to overtime, night work or long business trips.
LAB-031.e: True, unless the employee agrees (Article 137 of the 2019 Labour Code).
LAB-031.x:
Basis: Article 137 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Pregnant women from month 7 (month 6 in remote, border or island areas) may not be assigned overtime, night work or distant travel – unless they agree. A maternity protection measure.

LAB-032.q: Enterprises organising overtime must have the employee's consent.
LAB-032.e: True, except in special cases under Article 108 of the 2019 Labour Code (disasters, epidemics, mobilisation orders…).
LAB-032.x:
Basis: Articles 107 and 108 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Overtime needs the employee's consent; exceptions are special cases (disasters, epidemics, mobilisation orders, protecting life and property…) under Article 108.

LAB-033.q: Match each region with the monthly minimum wage from 01/01/2026:
LAB-033.e: Decree 293/2025/ND-CP, an average increase of 7.2% over 2025.
LAB-033.x:
Basis: Decree 293/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Monthly minimum wages from 01/01/2026: region I 5,310,000; II 4,730,000; III 4,140,000; IV 3,700,000 VND – up 7.2% on average.

LAB-034.q: The Region I hourly minimum wage from 01/01/2026 is:
LAB-034.e: Region I 25,500; II 22,700; III 20,000; IV 17,800 VND/hour.
LAB-034.x:
Basis: Decree 293/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: 2026 hourly minimums: region I 25,500; II 22,700; III 20,000; IV 17,800 VND/hour – for part-time, hourly-paid workers.
Distractors: 23,800 is region I in 2025; 22,700 is region II; 27,000 has no basis.

LAB-035.x:
Basis: Decree 161/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: The base salary from 01/07/2026 is 2,530,000 VND/month (from 2,340,000 under Decree 73/2024) – for the public sector and as the social insurance reference (SI-080).
Distractors: 2,340,000 is the old level; 1,800,000 the 2023 level; 2,600,000 has no basis.

LAB-036.q: The regional minimum wage is the lowest pay for the simplest work under normal conditions and serves as the basis for agreeing and paying wages.
LAB-036.e: True under Articles 90 and 91 of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-036.x:
Basis: Articles 90 and 91 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. The regional minimum wage is the lowest pay for the simplest work in normal conditions, securing a minimum living standard; it underpins wage bargaining and is the contribution floor (SI-009).

LAB-037.q: Enterprises must build pay scales, salary tables and labour norms, consult the employee representative organisation and publish them at the workplace before applying them; registration with the labour authority is not required.
LAB-037.e: True under Article 93 of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-037.x:
Basis: Article 93 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Employers set their own pay scales and labour norms, consult the employee representative and publish them before use – no registration with the labour authority (unlike the 2012 Code).

LAB-038.q: Each time wages are paid, the enterprise must give employees a pay slip showing salary, overtime, night pay, deductions and their amounts (if any).
LAB-038.e: True under Article 95(3) of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-038.x:
Basis: Article 95(3) of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Each payday the employer gives a payslip showing wages, overtime, night pay and deductions – transparency and supporting evidence for CIT-deductible payroll.

LAB-039.q: If wages are paid 15 days or more late, the enterprise must compensate the employee at least:
o: Interest on the late amount at the 1-month term deposit rate
Nothing if there is a reason
LAB-039.x:
Basis: Article 97 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Paying wages 15 or more days late (for force majeure, at most 30 days) requires compensation at least equal to interest at the 1-month deposit rate of the payroll bank.
Distractors: B, C and D have no basis.

LAB-040.q: The maximum monthly wage deduction to compensate for damage caused by the employee is:
o: 30% of monthly net pay after SI, HI, UI and PIT
LAB-040.x:
Basis: Article 102 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Deductions to compensate damage are capped at 30% of monthly net pay after social, health and unemployment insurance and PIT; the employee must be told why.
Distractors: B, C and D are wrong limits.

LAB-041.q: An employee's monthly net pay after insurance and PIT is VND 12 million. What is the maximum monthly deduction for damages (VND)?
LAB-041.x:
Basis: Labour Code 2019 Art. 102 (wage deductions), Art. 129 (compensation for damage).
Working: Maximum deduction = 30% of monthly net pay after social, health, unemployment insurance and PIT = 12,000,000 × 30% = 3,600,000 VND/month.
Analysis: Deductions compensate damage to tools, equipment or property, and the employee must be told why. For minor negligent damage worth up to 10 months of regional minimum wage, compensation is capped at 3 months' pay.
Check: 3,600,000 / 12,000,000 = 30% ✓.

LAB-042.q: Tet bonuses and the 13th-month salary are mandatory obligations under the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-042.e: False. Bonuses are decided by the employer based on business results and performance, under the bonus policy (Article 104).
LAB-042.x:
Basis: Article 104 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: False. Bonuses (including Tet and '13th-month') are employer decisions based on results and the bonus policy, not statutory duties. If promised in a contract or collective agreement, they become contractual obligations.

LAB-043.q: The bonus policy is decided by the employer and published at the workplace after consulting the employee representative organisation (if any).
LAB-043.e: True under Article 104 of the 2019 Labour Code. Bonuses may be in cash, assets or other forms.
LAB-043.x:
Basis: Article 104 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. The bonus policy is decided by the employer and published after consulting the employee representative (if any); bonuses may be cash, assets or other forms.

LAB-044.q: Work stoppage due to power/water failures not caused by the enterprise: for stoppages of 14 working days or less, stoppage pay is agreed but not below the minimum wage.
LAB-044.e: True under Article 99 of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-044.x:
Basis: Article 99(3) of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Stoppages from power or water failures not caused by the employer, disasters, epidemics…: for ≤ 14 working days, stoppage pay is agreed but not below the minimum wage; beyond 14 days it's agreed, with the first 14 still at least the minimum.

LAB-045.q: For work stoppages caused by the employer, employees are paid their full contractual salary.
LAB-045.e: True under Article 99(1) of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-045.x:
Basis: Article 99(1) of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Stoppages caused by the employer mean full contractual pay. If caused by the employee, that employee isn't paid.

LAB-046.q: Enterprises may pay wages in cash or via the employee's bank account; if via bank, the enterprise bears account opening and transfer fees.
LAB-046.e: True under Article 96 of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-046.x:
Basis: Article 96 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Wages may be paid in cash or to the employee's account; with bank payment, the employer bears account-opening and transfer fees. For tax, bank payment provides clear evidence.

LAB-047.q: Select ALL prohibited employer conduct in paying wages:
o: Restricting or interfering with how employees spend their wages
Forcing employees to spend wages on the enterprise's goods/services
Fining or cutting wages instead of disciplinary action
Paying wages via bank account as agreed
LAB-047.e: Articles 94 and 127 of the 2019 Labour Code prohibit interfering with wage spending and using fines or wage cuts instead of discipline.
LAB-047.x:
Basis: Articles 94 and 127 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Prohibited: (A) restricting or interfering with how employees spend wages; (B) forcing purchases from the employer; (C) fines or pay cuts in place of discipline.
Distractors: (D) Agreed bank payment is lawful (LAB-046).

LAB-048.q: An enterprise in Region II must pay unskilled workers (simplest jobs) in 2026 at least:
LAB-048.e: The 2026 Region II minimum wage under Decree 293/2025/ND-CP.
LAB-048.x:
Basis: Decree 293/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Unskilled workers doing simple work in region II in 2026 must earn at least 4,730,000 VND/month.
Distractors: 5,310,000 is region I; 4,140,000 region III; 2,530,000 the base salary.

LAB-049.q: From how many employees must an enterprise issue written internal labour regulations?
LAB-049.e: Article 118 of the 2019 Labour Code; enterprises with 10 or more must register them with the provincial labour authority.
LAB-049.x:
Basis: Articles 118 and 119 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Employers with 10 or more employees must issue written work rules and register them with the provincial labour authority; below 10, writing isn't mandatory but terms should be in contracts.
Distractors: 50, 100 and 5 are wrong.

LAB-050.q: Select ALL forms of labour discipline under the 2019 Labour Code:
o: Extension of the salary increase period by up to 6 months
LAB-050.e: Fines and wage cuts in lieu of discipline are prohibited.
LAB-050.x:
Basis: Article 124 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Four disciplinary forms: (A) reprimand; (B) deferring a pay rise by up to 6 months; (C) demotion; (D) dismissal.
Distractors: (E) Fines or pay deductions are prohibited (Article 127).

LAB-051.q: The limitation period for disciplining violations directly related to finance, assets or disclosure of technology/business secrets is:
LAB-051.e: The usual period is 6 months; violations related to finance, assets or secrets have 12 months (Article 123).
LAB-051.x:
Basis: Article 123 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Disciplinary limitation: normally 6 months from the violation; for violations directly involving finances, assets or disclosure of technology or business secrets: 12 months.
Distractors: 6 months is the normal period; 24 and 3 months are wrong.
Note: Fraud discovered after 12 months may be beyond discipline – timely audits and reconciliations matter.

LAB-052.q: Select ALL cases in which the enterprise may dismiss an employee:
o: Theft, embezzlement, intentional injury, drug use at work
Disclosing business or technology secrets causing serious damage
Absence without good reason for 5 cumulative days in 30 days or 20 cumulative days in 365 days
Arriving late twice in a month
LAB-052.e: Article 125 of the 2019 Labour Code; ordinary lateness is handled more lightly under internal regulations.
LAB-052.x:
Basis: Article 125 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Dismissal applies for: (A) theft, embezzlement, gambling, deliberate injury, drug use at work; (B) disclosing business or technology secrets causing serious damage; (C) unauthorised absence of 5 cumulative days in 30 or 20 in 365 without good reason (also sexual harassment, repeat offences while under pay deferral or demotion).
Distractors: (D) Ordinary lateness is handled more lightly under the work rules.

LAB-053.q: In disciplining, the enterprise must prove the employee's fault and involve the grassroots employee representative organisation of which the employee is a member.
LAB-053.e: True under Article 122 of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-053.x:
Basis: Article 122 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Disciplinary principles: the employer proves fault; the employee representative (if a member) participates; the employee may defend or be represented; minutes are kept. Procedural gaps can make dismissal unlawful.

LAB-054.q: Match the individual labour dispute mechanism with its limitation period:
LAB-054.e: Article 190 of the 2019 Labour Code, counted from discovery of the infringement.
LAB-054.x:
Basis: Article 190 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Limitation periods for individual labour disputes, from discovery of the violation: labour mediator 6 months; labour arbitration council 9 months; court 1 year.

LAB-055.q: Enterprises report labour changes to the labour authority periodically:
LAB-055.x:
Basis: Article 4 of Decree 145/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: Employers report workforce changes half-yearly (before 05/06) and annually (before 05/12) via the public service portal or the labour authority.
Distractors: B, C and D are wrong.

LAB-056.q: A collective labour agreement has a term of 1 to 3 years.
LAB-056.e: True under Article 78 of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-056.x:
Basis: Article 78 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Collective agreements last 1 to 3 years; a first-time agreement may be shorter. Terms more favourable than the law are binding (e.g., bonuses, allowances).

LAB-057.q: Trade-union fees payable by enterprises equal:
o: 2% of the payroll used for SI contributions
LAB-057.e: 2024 Trade Union Law; also applies to enterprises without a grassroots union.
LAB-057.x:
Basis: Trade Union Law 50/2024/QH15; Decree 105/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: The union fee = 2% of the social insurance salary fund, payable even without a grassroots union (LAB-090).
Distractors: B confuses it with members' 1% dues; C and D have no basis.

LAB-058.q: A company's SI payroll for October 2026 is VND 500 million. What trade-union fee is due this month (VND)?
LAB-058.x:
Basis: Law 50/2024/QH15; Decree 105/2026/ND-CP.
Working: 500,000,000 × 2% = 10,000,000 VND, due by 30/11/2026 (LAB-060), CIT-deductible (LAB-064).

LAB-059.q: Trade Union Law No. 50/2024/QH15 takes effect on:
LAB-059.e: The 2024 Trade Union Law was passed on 27/11/2024 and takes effect on 01/7/2025.
LAB-059.x:
Basis: Trade Union Law 50/2024/QH15.
Analysis: Passed 27/11/2024, effective 01/07/2025 (the same day as the 2024 Social Insurance Law).
Distractors: D is the passing date; B and C are wrong.

LAB-060.q: Under Decree 105/2026/ND-CP, the deadline for monthly trade-union fee payment is:
o: The last day of the following month
The last day of the quarter
LAB-060.e: Decree 105/2026/ND-CP (effective 16/5/2026) sets the payment deadline, which Decree 191/2013/ND-CP did not.
LAB-060.x:
Basis: Decree 105/2026/ND-CP (effective 16/05/2026).
Analysis: Monthly union fees are due by the last day of the following month – aligned with social insurance (SI-012); Decree 191/2013 was silent on this.
Distractors: B, C and D are wrong.

LAB-061.q: Agricultural, forestry, fishery and salt enterprises paying wages by production cycle may choose to pay trade-union fees monthly or every 3 months (registered with the union).
LAB-061.e: True under Article 4 of Decree 105/2026/ND-CP — directly applicable to livestock enterprises.
LAB-061.x:
Basis: Article 4 of Decree 105/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Agriculture, forestry, fishery and salt enterprises paying wages by production cycle may pay monthly or quarterly (registered with the union) – matching seasonal cash flows (e.g., livestock firms – LAB-091).

LAB-062.q: Under Decree 105/2026/ND-CP, if an enterprise still fails to pay, underpays, or pays for fewer employees than required more than 60 days after the deadline, it is deemed non-payment of trade-union fees.
LAB-062.e: True (Article 6 of Decree 105/2026/ND-CP). Within the first 60 days it is late payment; beyond 60 days, or not accruing/paying from the outset, is non-payment.
LAB-062.x:
Basis: Article 6 of Decree 105/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Within 60 days of the deadline it's late payment (LAB-101); beyond 60 days unpaid, underpaid or covering too few workers – or never accrued – is 'non-payment', a heavier violation.

LAB-063.q: An enterprise that suspends operations for 30 days or more with at least 50% of SI-covered employees laid off temporarily, or loses over 50% of total assets due to disasters, fire, epidemics or crop failure, may have trade-union fees suspended for up to 12 months.
LAB-063.e: True under Article 13 of Decree 105/2026/ND-CP. Article 12 also allows reducing the fee by up to 20% for up to 6 months when the enterprise cuts staff.
LAB-063.x:
Basis: Articles 12 and 13 of Decree 105/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Payments may be suspended up to 12 months when operations stop for 30+ days with ≥ 50% of insured staff laid off, or > 50% of assets are lost to disasters, fire, epidemics or crop failure. Article 12 also allows up to a 20% cut for up to 6 months during downsizing.

LAB-064.q: Statutory trade-union fees are deductible for CIT.
LAB-064.e: True, with payment documents as prescribed.
LAB-064.x:
Basis: Law 50/2024/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The 2% union fee is a statutory obligation, CIT-deductible with payment evidence (CIT-063).

LAB-065.q: An employee who unlawfully terminates the contract (insufficient notice) receives no severance and must pay half a month's salary plus salary for the days of notice not given.
LAB-065.e: True under Article 40 of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-065.x:
Basis: Articles 39 and 40 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Unlawful resignation (insufficient notice): no severance; compensation of half a month's pay plus pay for the unnoticed days; training costs repaid if applicable.

LAB-066.q: An enterprise that unlawfully terminates a contract must reinstate the employee, pay salary and insurance for the days not worked and pay at least 2 extra months' salary.
LAB-066.e: True under Article 41 of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-066.x:
Basis: Article 41 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. An employer's unlawful termination requires reinstatement, back pay and insurance for the days missed, plus at least 2 months' pay; extra compensation applies if no position remains or the employee won't return (LAB-098).

LAB-067.q: On leaving, an employee has 4 untaken days of annual leave; the daily contractual salary is VND 600,000. How much must the enterprise pay for the untaken days (VND)?
LAB-067.x:
Basis: Article 113(3) of the 2019 Labour Code.
Working: 4 days × 600,000 = 2,400,000 VND, PIT-exempt within labour-law limits (PIT-035).

LAB-068.q: The employer sets the annual leave schedule after consulting employees and must notify them in advance.
LAB-068.e: True under Article 113(4) of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-068.x:
Basis: Article 113(4) of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. The employer sets the annual leave schedule after consulting employees and gives notice – balancing production plans with leave rights.

LAB-069.q: Employees may agree with the employer to take annual leave in several parts or combine leave for up to 3 years at once.
LAB-069.e: True under Article 113(4) of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-069.x:
Basis: Article 113(4) of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Employees may agree to split annual leave or combine up to 3 years' leave at once.

LAB-070.q: The minimum weekly rest under the 2019 Labour Code is:
o: At least 24 consecutive hours per week; if impossible, an average of at least 4 days per month
LAB-070.x:
Basis: Article 111 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Weekly rest is at least 24 consecutive hours; if impossible (production cycles), at least 4 days a month on average.
Distractors: B and C have wrong hours; D – employers set the day, not the minimum.

LAB-071.q: Female employees get 30 minutes per day during menstruation (at least 3 days/month) and those raising children under 12 months get 60 minutes per day, with full pay.
LAB-071.e: True under Article 137 of the 2019 Labour Code and Decree 145/2020/ND-CP.
LAB-071.x:
Basis: Article 137 of the 2019 Labour Code; Decree 145/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Women get 30 minutes a day during menstruation (at least 3 days a month) and 60 minutes a day while nursing a child under 12 months – fully paid. Denial can be fined under Decree 283/2026 (LAB-078).

LAB-072.q: If a labour contract expires while a female employee is pregnant or raising a child under 12 months, she has priority for a new contract.
LAB-072.e: True under Article 137(4) of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-072.x:
Basis: Article 137(4) of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. If a contract expires during pregnancy or while nursing a child under 12 months, the woman has priority for a new contract – an anti-discrimination measure.

LAB-073.q: Employers must hold periodic workplace dialogue at least once a year.
LAB-073.e: True under Article 63 of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-073.x:
Basis: Article 63 of the 2019 Labour Code; Decree 145/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Periodic workplace dialogue at least once a year; also on request or when issues arise (mass layoffs, pay scales…).

LAB-074.q: If an employee cannot receive wages directly, the employer may pay a person lawfully authorised by the employee.
LAB-074.e: True under Article 94 of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-074.x:
Basis: Article 94 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Wages are paid directly, fully and on time; if the employee can't collect, a lawfully authorised person may. Internal control: keep authorisations to prevent ghost payroll.

LAB-075.q: An employee lawfully dismissed still receives severance for periods not covered by UI.
LAB-075.e: False. Severance does not apply to dismissal or to those eligible for a pension (Article 46).
LAB-075.x:
Basis: Article 46 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: False. Severance doesn't apply to dismissed employees or those eligible for a pension – even for uninsured periods.

LAB-076.q: Decree 283/2026/ND-CP (effective 10/9/2026) replaces Decree 12/2022/ND-CP on administrative penalties in labour and SI.
LAB-076.e: True. Decree 283/2026/ND-CP was issued on 15/7/2026 and applies to all employers in Vietnam.
LAB-076.x:
Basis: Decree 283/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Decree 283/2026 (issued 15/07/2026, effective 10/09/2026) replaces Decree 12/2022 on labour, social insurance and overseas-worker penalties (SI-071).

LAB-077.q: Per reports on Decree 283/2026/ND-CP, paying probation wages below 85% of the job salary is fined up to (individual level):
LAB-077.e: Probation pay must be at least 85% of the job salary (Article 26, Labour Code 2019); violations are fined up to 10 million, double for organisations.
LAB-077.x:
Basis: Decree 283/2026/ND-CP; Article 26 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Paying probation wages below 85% of the job's pay is fined up to 10 million VND (individual level; organisations double), plus paying the shortfall.
Distractors: 40, 75 and 2 million relate to other violations.

LAB-078.q: Under Decree 283/2026/ND-CP, not allowing a female employee raising a child under 12 months a 60-minute daily break may be fined up to VND 40 million.
LAB-078.e: True per reports on the new fines; the 60-minute paid break is in Article 137 of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-078.x:
Basis: Decree 283/2026/ND-CP; Article 137 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Denying nursing mothers their paid 60 minutes a day can be fined up to 40 million VND under the new penalties – reflecting the priority on maternity protection.

LAB-079.q: An employee worked 10 years, 7 of them covered by UI; average salary for the last 6 months was VND 18 million; the contract expired. What is the severance allowance (VND)?
LAB-079.e: Qualifying period = 10 − 7 = 3 years; allowance = 3 × ½ × 18 = 27 million VND.
LAB-079.x:
Basis: Labour Code 2019 Art. 46 (severance allowance); Decree 145/2020/ND-CP Art. 8.
Working: Countable service = total service − time under unemployment insurance = 10 − 7 = 3 years; allowance = 3 × ½ month × 18 million = 27 million VND.
Analysis: Each year earns half a month's average pay of the 6 months before leaving. Unemployment-insured time is excluded because the worker draws unemployment benefits from the fund. Contract expiry is a lawful termination (Art. 34), so severance applies. Statutory severance isn't subject to PIT.

LAB-080.q: An employee loses their job due to restructuring; the qualifying period is 1 year and the 6-month average salary is VND 12 million. What is the job-loss allowance (VND)?
LAB-080.e: One month per year = 12 million but at least two months' salary → 24 million VND.
LAB-080.x:
Basis: Article 47 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Working: 1 year × 1 month's pay = 12 million < the 2-month minimum → 2 × 12 = 24 million VND.

LAB-081.q: A worker (VND 40,000/hour) works 3 hours of overtime at night on a normal day, having worked normal hours during the day. What is the minimum overtime pay (150% + 30% + 20% × 150%) (VND)?
LAB-081.x:
Basis: Article 98 of the 2019 Labour Code; Decree 145/2020/ND-CP.
Working: Night overtime on a weekday = 150% (overtime) + 30% (night) + 20% × 150% (night-overtime premium) = 210%. Pay = 40,000 × 210% × 3 = 252,000 VND.

LAB-082.q: In 2026, Vietnam Culture Day (24/11) falls on a Tuesday. Employees working that day are paid at least:
LAB-082.e: 24/11 is a paid public holiday from 2026; working on a holiday earns at least 300% (excluding holiday pay).
o: 300% of hourly pay for hours worked, excluding holiday pay
LAB-082.x:
Basis: Resolution 28/2026/QH16; Article 98 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: From 2026, 24/11 is a paid holiday (LAB-026); working that day earns at least 300% per hour, plus holiday pay (≥ 400% in total).
Distractors: B, C and D are weekday or weekly-rest rates, or ignore the holiday.

LAB-083.q: If a public holiday coincides with the weekly day off, employees get a compensatory day off on the next working day.
LAB-083.e: True under Article 111(3) of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-083.x:
Basis: Article 111(3) of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. If a holiday falls on the weekly rest day, employees get the next working day off.

LAB-084.q: A part-time worker in Region I works 80 hours in a month. What is the minimum pay under the 2026 hourly minimum wage (VND)?
LAB-084.x:
Basis: Decree 293/2025/ND-CP (2026 hourly minimum – per the question); Labour Code 2019 Art. 91.
Working: Region I hourly minimum = 25,500 VND; 80 hours × 25,500 = 2,040,000 VND.
Analysis: The hourly minimum applies to hourly-paid (part-time) workers; agreed pay can't be lower. The region I monthly minimum of 5,310,000 corresponds to about 208 hours – the hourly rate is set accordingly.
Note: The 2026 minimums follow the question's basis – check the original.

LAB-085.q: The salary by job or title for the simplest work under normal conditions and full working time must not be below the minimum wage.
LAB-085.e: True. The minimum wage is the floor; trained jobs are no longer required to be 7% higher as before, but pay must reflect productivity and quality.
LAB-085.x:
Basis: Articles 90 and 91 of the 2019 Labour Code; Decree 293/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Pay for the simplest full-time work may not fall below the minimum wage. The old rule requiring trained workers to earn at least 7% more was dropped; employers design pay scales around productivity and quality.

LAB-086.q: Select ALL mandatory main contents of a labour contract under Article 21 of the 2019 Labour Code:
LAB-086.e: The bank account number is not a mandatory contract content.
o: Salary, payment method and timing, allowances and additions
Promotion and pay rises; working and rest hours
LAB-086.x:
Basis: Article 21 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Key contract terms: (A) job and place; (B) duration; (C) pay, payment method and timing, allowances, supplements; (D) promotion and pay rises; hours and rest (plus protective equipment, social insurance, training…).
Distractors: (E) A bank account number isn't mandatory.

LAB-087.q: When an employee reaches retirement age and has enough SI years for a pension, the employer may unilaterally terminate the contract (unless otherwise agreed).
LAB-087.e: True under Article 36(1)(đ) of the 2019 Labour Code.
LAB-087.x:
Basis: Article 36(1)(đ) of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Reaching retirement age with pension eligibility is a ground for the employer to terminate (unless otherwise agreed).

LAB-088.q: An employer unilaterally terminating a 24-month fixed-term contract with an employee who regularly fails to complete work (valid ground) must give notice of at least:
LAB-088.e: Fixed-term contracts of 12 to 36 months: at least 30 days' notice (Article 36, 2019 Labour Code).
LAB-088.x:
Basis: Article 36(2) of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: For 12–36-month contracts, the employer gives at least 30 days' notice when lawfully terminating (persistent non-performance under the evaluation policy).
Distractors: 45 days is for indefinite contracts; 3 working days for under 12 months; 120 days for certain special sectors.

LAB-089.q: An agricultural processing enterprise may organise up to 300 overtime hours per year. A worker has done 260 hours by the end of October 2026. What is the maximum remaining overtime for the last 2 months (monthly limit 40 hours) (hours)?
LAB-089.e: Annual remainder 300 − 260 = 40 hours; monthly limits 40 × 2 = 80, so the annual cap governs: 40 hours.
LAB-089.x:
Basis: Article 107 of the 2019 Labour Code; Decree 145/2020/ND-CP.
Working: Annual room = 300 − 260 = 40 hours; monthly room = 40 × 2 = 80 hours. The tighter limit governs → at most 40 hours for the last two months.

LAB-090.q: Enterprises without a grassroots trade union must still pay the 2% trade-union fee.
LAB-090.e: True. The fee obligation does not depend on having a grassroots union.
LAB-090.x:
Basis: Law 50/2024/QH15; Decree 105/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The 2% union fee applies to all employers regardless of whether a grassroots union exists.

LAB-091.q: A livestock enterprise registers to pay trade-union fees every 3 months. SI payroll for July, August and September 2026 is 300, 320 and 280 million. What fee is due for this period (VND million)?
LAB-091.x:
Basis: Decree 105/2026/ND-CP (union fees – per the question); Trade Union Law 2024.
Working: Union fee = 2% of the insured payroll = (300 + 320 + 280) × 2% = 900 × 2% = 18 million VND, paid once for Q3.
Analysis: Agriculture, forestry, fisheries and salt firms paying by production cycle may register quarterly or half-yearly payment instead of monthly. The 2% fee is an employer cost (not deducted from wages), unlike the 1% member dues paid by union members.
Note: Decree 105/2026 is a 2026 text beyond my knowledge; the explanation follows the question's basis – verify against the original.

LAB-092.q: Match each item with the measure under the 2019 Labour Code:
LAB-092.e: Articles 124, 125 and 129 of the 2019 Labour Code: reprimand; extension of the salary-increase period up to 6 months; demotion; dismissal.
p: Absence for 5 cumulative days in 30 days without good reason
Disciplinary form lasting up to 6 months
Minor first breach of internal rules
Compensation per internal rules (max 3 months' salary if under 10 months' regional minimum wage)
LAB-092.x:
Basis: Articles 124, 125 and 129 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Unauthorised absence of 5 cumulative days in 30 → possible dismissal (LAB-052). Time-limited discipline up to 6 months → deferred pay rise. Minor first offence → reprimand. Minor negligent damage (below 10 months' regional minimum wage) → compensation per work rules, up to 3 months' pay.

LAB-093.q: Discipline may not be imposed on an employee on sick leave, convalescence or leave approved by the employer.
LAB-093.e: True under Article 122(4) of the 2019 Labour Code; if the limitation period has expired meanwhile, it is extended by up to 60 days.
LAB-093.x:
Basis: Article 122(4) of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Discipline can't proceed against employees on sick leave, convalescence, approved leave, in detention, pregnant or on maternity leave…; if the limitation lapses meanwhile, it extends by up to 60 days.

LAB-094.q: An employee in normal conditions started on 01/3/2026. How many days of annual leave (pro-rated) do they get for 2026 (12 days × months worked / 12)?
LAB-094.x:
Basis: Article 113 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Working: Starting 01/03/2026 → 10 months worked (March–December). Pro-rata leave = 12 × 10 / 12 = 10 days.

LAB-095.q: Consider these statements on labour relations in 2026:
LAB-095.e: Minimum probation pay is 85%; fines or wage cuts in lieu of discipline are prohibited.
o: 2026 has 12 paid public holiday and Tet days.
Minimum probation pay is 70% of the job salary.
The base salary from 01/7/2026 is VND 2.53 million.
Enterprises may fine employees for arriving late.
LAB-095.x:
Basis: 2019 Labour Code; Resolution 28/2026/QH16; Decree 161/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) True – 12 paid holidays from 2026 (LAB-025). (2) False – probation pay is at least 85%. (3) True – base salary 2.53 million from 01/07/2026. (4) False – fines in place of discipline are banned (LAB-047).

LAB-096.q: Per reports on Decree 283/2026/ND-CP, deducting wages for lateness (instead of disciplinary action) may be fined up to VND 40 million.
LAB-096.e: True. Fining or cutting wages in lieu of discipline is prohibited by Article 127 of the 2019 Labour Code and penalised more heavily under Decree 283/2026.
LAB-096.x:
Basis: Decree 283/2026/ND-CP; Article 127 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. Deducting pay for lateness is a fine in place of discipline – banned and finable up to 40 million VND under Decree 283/2026. Use work-rule discipline or attendance bonuses (rewarding punctuality instead of penalising lateness).

LAB-097.q: Monthly-paid wages are paid once a month or twice a month; the payment time is agreed and must be fixed at:
LAB-097.e: Article 97 of the 2019 Labour Code: the payment time is fixed at a periodic point.
o: Any day the enterprise has cash
LAB-097.x:
Basis: Article 97 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: Monthly wages are paid monthly or twice a month; the date is agreed and fixed periodically (e.g., the 5th of each month).
Distractors: B, C and D lack periodicity and breach the rule.

LAB-098.q: An enterprise unlawfully terminates an employee earning VND 20 million/month. Apart from wages and insurance for the days not worked, what minimum additional amount must the enterprise pay under Article 41 of the Labour Code (VND million)?
LAB-098.e: Under Article 41 of the 2019 Labour Code, at least 2 extra months' salary: 2 × 20 = 40 million VND.
LAB-098.x:
Basis: Article 41 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Working: Besides back pay and insurance, at least 2 months' pay: 2 × 20 = 40 million VND. If the employee won't return, severance and any agreed extra apply.

LAB-099.q: During probation, the employee may terminate unilaterally without notice and without compensation.
LAB-099.e: True. During probation, either party may cancel the probation agreement without notice or compensation (Article 27).
LAB-099.x:
Basis: Article 27 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Analysis: True. During probation either party may end it without notice or compensation – the nature of a trial.

LAB-100.q: The maximum total of normal and overtime hours in a day (weekly scheduling) is:
LAB-100.e: Overtime may not exceed 50% of normal daily hours; under weekly scheduling the total may not exceed 12 hours per day (Article 107 Labour Code, Decree 145/2020).
LAB-100.x:
Basis: Article 107 of the 2019 Labour Code; Decree 145/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: On a weekly schedule, normal plus overtime hours may not exceed 12 a day.
Distractors: 10 hours is the normal-hours limit on weekly schedules; 14 and 16 exceed limits.

LAB-101.q: Under Decree 105/2026/ND-CP, an enterprise that has not paid the full trade-union fee within 60 days after the deadline is deemed to be paying late.
LAB-101.e: True. Beyond 60 days (or not accruing/paying from the outset) is non-payment (Article 6).
LAB-101.x:
Basis: Article 6 of Decree 105/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Within 60 days after the deadline, an unpaid balance is 'late'; beyond 60 days (or never accrued) it is 'non-payment' (LAB-062).

LAB-102.q: Select ALL correct statements on the 2026 regional minimum wages (Decree 293/2025/ND-CP):
LAB-102.e: The SI/HI cap uses the reference level (equal to the base salary); the regional minimum wage is the SI floor and the basis of the UI cap.
o: The regional minimum wage replaces the base salary in computing the SI cap
LAB-102.x:
Basis: Decree 293/2025/ND-CP; Law 41/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True: (A) region I 5,310,000; (B) region IV 3,700,000; (C) region III hourly minimum 20,000 VND.
Distractors: (D) The social/health cap uses the reference level (base salary); the regional minimum is the contribution floor and the unemployment cap basis (SI-044).

LAB-103.e: Procedure under Article 122 of the 2019 Labour Code and Article 70 of Decree 145/2020/ND-CP.
o: Record the violation and gather evidence
Notify the employee and representative organisation of the disciplinary meeting (at least 5 working days before)
Hold the disciplinary meeting and record minutes
Issue the disciplinary decision within the limitation period
Send the decision to the parties concerned
LAB-103.x:
Basis: Article 122 of the 2019 Labour Code; Article 70 of Decree 145/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) Record the violation and gather evidence → (2) notify the employee and representative at least 5 working days ahead → (3) hold the meeting with minutes → (4) issue the decision within the limitation period → (5) send it to the parties. Procedural errors can void the decision.

LAB-104.q: An enterprise with 1,000 or more female employees that does not provide a room for expressing and storing breast milk may be fined up to VND 40 million under Decree 283/2026/ND-CP.
LAB-104.e: True per the published new fines; the obligation comes from Decree 145/2020/ND-CP.
LAB-104.x:
Basis: Decree 283/2026/ND-CP; Decree 145/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Employers with 1,000 or more female workers must provide a lactation room (Decree 145/2020); failure can be fined up to 40 million VND under the new penalties.

LAB-105.q: An employee earning VND 24 million/month (26 standard days) takes 3 days of personal leave for their own wedding. How much must the enterprise pay for these 3 days (rounded to VND)?
LAB-105.e: Own marriage: 3 days fully paid: 24,000,000 / 26 × 3 ≈ 2,769,231 VND.
LAB-105.x:
Basis: Article 115 of the 2019 Labour Code.
Working: 3 days' paid marriage leave: 24,000,000 / 26 × 3 = 2,769,230.77 ≈ 2,769,231 VND.
Note: The 26 standard days come from the pay policy; using the month's actual working days may change the result.
